missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Час' is the masculine nominative subject. 'Поздний' is the agreeing adjective, and 'уже' adds the time nuance.
Strategic focus: Accusative of duration. 'Час' is the accusative expressing how long the waiting lasted. 'Целый' agrees in the masculine accusative.
Strategic focus: Genitive after numeral. 'Часа' is the genitive singular required after 'два'. 'Прошло' is the neuter impersonal verb.

missions.phrase: К этому часу всё будет готово.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Dative after preposition. 'Часу' is the dative form after 'к' to express a deadline. 'Этому' agrees in the masculine dative.
Strategic focus: Instrumental after preposition. 'Часом' is instrumental after 'с' to mean with each passing hour. 'Каждым' agrees in the masculine instrumental.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'Часе' is the prepositional form after 'в' marking what the hour contains. 'Шестьдесят минут' uses the genitive plural.
Strategic focus: Accusative after preposition. 'Час' is the accusative after 'через' to mean in an hour's time; the form matches the nominative. A very common phrase.

missions.phrase: Магазин работает круглые сутки и часы.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative plural. 'Часы' is the nominative plural here meaning hours of operation. 'Круглые' agrees in the plural, and 'работает' is the verb.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural of quantity. 'Часов' is the genitive plural after 'несколько'. 'Подряд' adds the sense of continuity.
Strategic focus: Nominative for telling time. 'Час' is nominative singular after 'один' to state one o'clock. 'Ровно' means exactly.
